## Description
&#10;&#9;&#9;The following forms of potassium may exist on Mars :&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9; 1. K⁺ in silicate lattices — plagioclase (the ~0.2–0.5 wt% K₂O discussed earlier), K-feldspar &#10;&#9;   (sanidine/microcline in more evolved rocks), micas (phlogopite, biotite)&#10;     2. KCl — in evaporite/sulfate deposits (e.g., Valles Marineris, Terra Cimmeria); detected by &#10;        orbital CRISM/OMEGA&#10;     3. K-bearing smectites (nontronite) — in Gale and Jezero Crater sediments&#10;&#10;&#9;&#9;So potassium is abundant (~2.5–3.5 wt% K₂O in bulk crustal rock), but exclusively as K⁺ &#10;&#9;&#9;in crystal structures or halide salts — never as a free oxide or peroxide phase.&#10;&#9;
